entries.headline: Well Up announced for Steam on January 19, 2027
entries.summary: AUTOMATON reports that OOPS.K has announced Well Up, a first-person climbing game planned for PC via Steam on January 19, 2027. Players control each hand separately to climb an old rope that can slip or break.

entries.headline: Rain98 releases a free Steam demo with roughly three hours of play
entries.summary: A developer announcement carried by Denfaminicogamer says Rain98 released a free Steam demo on October 17. It covers the opening through the first part of Chapter 2, offering roughly three hours of story, character interaction and exploration in 1998 Tokyo.

entries.headline: CRYMELIGHT producer says its story is independent of CRYSTAR and CRYMACHINA
entries.summary: In an AUTOMATON interview, producer and director Takumi Isobe describes CRYMELIGHT as a standalone game with no direct story connection to CRYSTAR or CRYMACHINA. The team aims to distinguish its roguelike action game through its narrative.

entries.headline: Analysis suggests declining Steam wishlist conversion ratios
entries.summary: AUTOMATON discusses Chris Zukowski’s analysis of sales data from 160 games. In the later release cohort, median sales-to-launch-wishlist ratios at one and six months were roughly half those of the earlier cohort. These are sample-based marketing findings, not Steam-wide statistics.

entries.headline: Planet Zoo study links play with higher conservation donations
entries.summary: AUTOMATON discusses an Oxford research team’s study of 545 respondents. Planet Zoo players donated roughly twice as much on average as non-players, while play was also associated with animal knowledge and related measures. The paper is an unreviewed preprint, and the associations do not establish causation.

entries.summary: AUTOMATON reports that BULKHEAD is withdrawing XP and cash bonuses recently introduced for the blue team during WARDOGS Season 2. The report concerns a balance adjustment; the game is available in Steam Early Access.

entries.headline: Mimic Busters launches on Steam with player-made disguises
entries.summary: Denfaminicogamer reports that Mimic Busters, developed by DevAdam and Tape Corps and published by GameDev.ist, launched on PC via Steam on October 16. Hiders shape and paint a cube into a disguise resembling objects in the environment to evade hunters online.

entries.headline: AMPANIC launches on Steam, turning shopkeeping into an aiming game
entries.summary: A developer announcement carried by Denfaminicogamer says YuLu released AMPANIC for Windows on Steam on October 16. Gathering, processing, mixing and serving rely on mouse aiming. The game supports online co-op and a competitive mode that sends customers to an opponent.

entries.headline: GTA6 Japanese store pages display a CERO Z rating
entries.summary: Denfaminicogamer reports on October 17 that GTA6’s Japanese PlayStation and Xbox store pages display a CERO Z rating for ages 18 and over, with crime and violence descriptors. Differences in content between Japanese and overseas versions had not been established.
